dataIdInfo.idAbs:
These sets of data include the drinking water supply management area boundaries and the vulnerability levels within each management area in Minnesota. More information can be found at: https://www.health.state.mn.us/communities/environment/water/swp/reqrec.html Follow the links below to the access the individual metadata pages for each layer: Drinking Water Supply Management Areas: drinking_water_supply_management_areas.html Drinking Water Supply Management Areas Vulnerability: drinking_water_supply_management_area_vulnerability.html

dataIdInfo.idPurp: This dataset was developed with the intention of protecting the public drinking water supply and complies with the federal Safe Drinking Water Act, United States Code, title 42 and the State of Minnesota Rule (parts 4720.5100 to 4720.5590).

edom.edomvd: Single capture zone for a given DWSMA
Multiple capture zones for a given DWSMA
Complex capture zones for a given DWSMA (overlapping or adjacent regions)

attr.attrdef: Date of DWSMA Approval. For multi-community DWSMAs; It is the final date that all pubic water suppliers signed the approval.
Acres of the DWSMA (derived from AREA / 4046.8717 ) + 0.001

Public Water Supply ID . The first digit is either a 1 or a 5. A 1 signifies it is a cummunity public water supplier. A 5 signifies it is a non-community public water supplier. The 2nd and 3rd digits are the county code. The last 4 digits are sequential as new public water suppliers are added.

enttyp.enttypd: Vulnerability of Public Water Supply Management Area

attr.attrdef: DWSMA Vulnerability Type Code - Whether the vulnerabilty of the DWSMA was determined from the SWCA or GWCA

edom.edomvd: Ground Water. The vulnerability is determined from only the GWCA
Surface Water - The vulnerability is determined from only the SWCA
The SWCA and GWCA overlap and the GWCA has a high vulnerability
The SWCA and GWCA overlap and the GWCA has a low or moderate vulnerability

attr.attrdef: Drinking Water Supply Management Area Vulnerability ID
DWSMA Vulnerability Code. Note* Very High and Very Low are no longer used

edom.edomvd: Very High - This is no longer used and should be considered High
Very Low - This is no lnger used and should be considred Low

attr.attrdef: DWSMA Vulnerability - The vulnerability of the DWSMA. Where the GWCA and SWCA overlap, the vulnerability is considered to be high becasue the SWCA is high

edom.edomvd: Very High Vulnerability. (This is no longer used and should be considered a High vulnerability)
Very Low Vulnerability (This is no longer used and should be considered a Low vulnerability)

attr.attrdef: Aquifer Vulnerability Code (for public and regulatory use) - Low is considered not vulnerable. Moderate and High are considered to be vulnerable.
Drinking Water Supply Management Area ID - sequential number
GWCA Vulnerability - The vulnerability of the GWCA may be differnet that the DWSMA vulnerability where the GWCA and SWCA overlap.

overview.eaover: Follow the links below to the access the individual meta data pages for each layer: Drinking Water Supply Management Areas: drinking_water_supply_management_areas.html In 2025 MDH began creating DWSMAs that included multiple public water suppliers where DWSMAs from individual public water suppliers extended into other public water suppliers DWSMAs. This was to address management ambiguity in areas where DWSMAs overlapped. For these DWSMAs, a "fake" pwsid is used in the attribute table to represent all public water suppliers. More information about how and why this was done can be found in the Drinking Water Supply Management Areas metadata.
